PART 2 — THE REPORT (the population the policy does not cover; operator: '4x4 go science probably requires many GB'). The §3.2 causal reading — resident set dominated by accumulated conversation context plus the peak of whatever the lane spawned — is a statement about AGENT lanes. Science rows (load a ~500 MB artifact, run a bitset Tarjan) are a different population, but the measured figures in this repository say the wall rule is still the safe DEFAULT for them: I5 at 4×4 (bitset/Tarjan, 2.8 GB RSS — docs/infra/property-ownership.md:115, instrument-coverage.md:216 T344), closure at 4×4 (600M children, 1.1 GB — instrument-coverage.md:225), vb_i11 exhaustive 4×4 (558 MB RSS — instrument-coverage.md:219 T473), oracle-4x4-v2.wzo2 on disk (494 MB measured 2026-08-25; the brief cites 518 MB). All four are long-running rows, so their walls land in the ≥1800 s band and they declare 4608 — which covers the largest measured (2.8 GB) with 1.8 GB headroom; the disk artifact is not RSS. VERDICT: wall-band declaration IS safe as the DEFAULT for type=battery rows, with two stated conditions: (a) the dispatcher must set --wall honestly — the wall is the declaration's input, and battery walls already track expected runtime; (b) 'safe default' means default, not ceiling — the policy's own escape hatch is the declared need: a battery row whose need exceeds its band declares --ram-mb=N with a logged reason (exactly the operator's 'require dispatch to set RAM requirements if tasks require more'). The failure modes of a wrong default are loud and labeled (admission refusal — row stays dispatchable — or a labeled RSS-cap death), never a silent wrong answer. What is NOT warranted: a science-specific default. Four points is not a distribution, and inventing a constant is the exact habit ram-policy.md was written to end. WHAT WOULD MEASURE IT: the same corpus §3.2 came from — a Track A 4×4 regeneration (or its closest tractable subset) run under tools/runner with a generous --ram-mb, its rss_mb entering untracked/runs/, plus the INV-4 declared_vs_actual loop (>125% overrun logged) re-deriving the band table once science rows are in the corpus. Caveat the policy itself states: rss_mb is max(peak_rss.values()) — the largest single member's peak — so a multi-process science run is UNDERSTATED by the field; for the measured rows the peak member is the compute process itself (Tarjan), so I5's 2.8 GB is the process's own RSS. This is a follow-up row's measurement, not this one's guess.

PROCESS NOTE (constraint 'land atomically'): bin/subagent was landed with three in-place edit calls, not copy-edit-verify-move. Between the signature change and the caller update the file would have crashed a concurrent dispatch (TypeError: _declared_ram_mb 3-vs-4 args) — a brief window on a file every lane uses, closed within minutes and verified by the full dispatch-lifecycle regression + smoke afterwards. The holds= field (bin/subagent) prevented a second writer, but not a second DISPATCHER. Copy-then-swap would have been strictly safer; recorded so the next row touching a dispatch-path file chooses it.
